original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
bhūya eva mahābāho śrṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ|
yatte'haṃ prīyamāṇāya vakṣyāmi hitakāmyayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Hear once more, mighty-armed one, my supreme word (paramaṃ vacaḥ), which I shall speak to you, who are taking delight [in it] (prīyamāṇa), out of a wish for your good.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prīyamāṇāya: 'to you who are delighted/pleased' (by hearing, as most take it); the verse does not say by what. 'bhūya eva' links the chapter back to the teaching of ch. 7–9 (cf. 9.34).

original.text:
na me viduḥ suragaṇāḥ prabhavaṃ na maharṣayaḥ|
ahamādirhi devānāṃ maharṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Neither the hosts of gods (sura) nor the great seers (maharṣi) know my coming-forth (prabhava); for I am in every way the origin (ādi) of the gods and of the great seers.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prabhava: 'origin, coming into being'; some commentators also allow the sense 'majesty, power' (prabhāva). The reason given ('for I am their origin') is the verse's own: what arose later cannot know what precedes it.

original.text:
yo māmajamanādiṃ ca vetti lokamaheśvaram|
asammūḍhaḥ sa martyeṣu sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: One who knows me as unborn (aja) and beginningless (anādi), the great lord of the world (lokamaheśvara) — he, undeluded (asammūḍha) among mortals, is freed from all sins (pāpa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The stated result (phala) of knowing the Lord as unborn and beginningless: freedom from delusion and from all sins. Cf. 4.6 (ajo 'pi san).

original.text:
buddhirjñānamasaṃmohaḥ kṣamā satyaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ|
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ bhavo'bhāvo bhayaṃ cābhayameva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Understanding (buddhi), knowledge (jñāna), freedom from delusion (asaṃmoha), forbearance (kṣamā), truth (satya), restraint (dama), calm (śama), pleasure and pain (sukha, duḥkha), coming-to-be and not-being (bhava, abhāva), fear and fearlessness (bhaya, abhaya) — [the sentence continues in 10.5].
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: First half of a two-verse list completed in 10.5 ('these various states of beings arise from me alone'). bhavo 'bhāvaḥ: taken by the commentators as birth/existence and its absence or destruction; the verse gives only the pair. dama and śama are both 'restraint/calm'; commentators commonly assign dama to the outer senses and śama to the inner faculty, which the verse does not state. buddhi is kept distinct from manas, citta and cetas.

original.text:
ahiṃsā samatā tuṣṭistapo dānaṃ yaśo'yaśaḥ|
bhavanti bhāvā bhūtānāṃ matta eva pṛthagvidhāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Non-harming (ahiṃsā), evenness (samatā), contentment (tuṣṭi), austerity (tapas), giving (dāna), fame and ill-fame (yaśas, ayaśas) — these states (bhāva) of beings, in their several kinds, arise from me alone.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Completes 10.4: twenty states in all, including opposites (pleasure and pain, fear and fearlessness, fame and ill-fame), are said to arise from the Lord alone (matta eva). The verse does not say how; commentators add 'according to their karma'. tuṣṭi here is contentment as a state of beings, not the Sāṃkhya 'nine complacencies'; bhāva here means 'states, dispositions' in general, not the Sāṃkhya eight bhāvas of buddhi.

original.text:
maharṣayaḥ sapta pūrve catvāro manavastathā|
madbhāvā mānasā jātā yeṣāṃ loka imāḥ prajāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: The seven great seers (maharṣi) and, of old, the four and the Manus (pūrve catvāro manavas — the grouping is construed in more than one way), sharing my being (madbhāva), were born of mind (mānasa); from them are these creatures in the world.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Construal divides: (a) 'the seven great seers of old and the four Manus'; (b) 'the seven great seers, the four earlier ones (taken by some as Sanaka and his brothers), and the Manus'. madbhāvāḥ: 'of my nature/being' or 'whose disposition is toward me'. mānasā jātāḥ: 'born from mind' — the verse does not say whose (the Lord's, or Brahmā's as in the Purāṇic accounts). The paraphrase keeps the minimal shared sense: progenitors of creatures born of mind, sharing the Lord's being.

original.text:
etāṃ vibhūtiṃ yogaṃ ca mama yo vetti tattvataḥ|
so'vikampena yogena yujyate nātra saṃśayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: One who knows in truth (tattvataḥ) this manifestation (vibhūti) and yoga of mine is joined with unwavering (avikampa) yoga; of this there is no doubt.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'yoga' is used twice with different subjects: the Lord's yoga (his power, cf. 'paśya me yogam aiśvaram' 9.5, 11.8) is the object known; the knower's 'unwavering yoga' is the result.

original.text:
ahaṃ sarvasya prabhavo mattaḥ sarvaṃ pravartate|
iti matvā bhajante māṃ budhā bhāvasamanvitāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: I am the source (prabhava) of all; from me everything proceeds. Thinking thus, the wise (budha), endowed with bhāva, worship (bhajante) me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: bhāvasamanvitāḥ: 'endowed with bhāva' — commentators divide between 'with devotion/love' and 'with conviction regarding the highest truth'. Worship is presented as following from understanding (iti matvā).

original.text:
maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam|
kathayantaśca māṃ nityaṃ tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: With their citta on me (maccitta), their prāṇa gone to me (madgataprāṇa), enlightening one another and always speaking of me, they are content and they delight.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: madgataprāṇāḥ: 'whose prāṇa has gone to me' — read by commentators either as 'whose life is given to me' or as 'whose vital powers/senses are absorbed in me'; the verse does not decide. citta is kept distinct from manas, buddhi and cetas.

original.text:
teṣāṃ satatayuktānāṃ bhajatāṃ prītipūrvakam|
dadāmi buddhiyogaṃ taṃ yena māmupayānti te
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: To them, ever joined (satatayukta), worshipping with love (prītipūrvakam), I give that yoga of understanding (buddhiyoga) by which they come to me.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The buddhiyoga here is given by the Lord to those already worshipping; cf. the buddhiyoga taught in 2.39–53. prītipūrvakam: 'with love/affection' (or 'with delight').

original.text:
teṣāmevānukampārthamahamajñānajaṃ tamaḥ|
nāśayāmyātmabhāvastho jñānadīpena bhāsvatā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Out of compassion (anukampā) for them alone, I, abiding in [the] ātmabhāva, destroy the darkness (tamas) born of ignorance (ajñāna) with the shining lamp of knowledge (jñāna).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmabhāvasthaḥ is ambiguous: 'dwelling within their being/inner faculty' or 'remaining in my own nature'; the commentators divide, and the paraphrase leaves it open. tamas here is 'darkness' born of ignorance, not named as the guṇa.

original.text:
paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma pavitraṃ paramaṃ bhavān|
puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyamādidevamajaṃ vibhum
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Arjuna said: You are the supreme brahman, the supreme abode (dhāman), the supreme purifier; the eternal, divine person (puruṣa), the first god, unborn (aja), all-pervading (vibhu) — [continued in 10.13].
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
āhustvāmṛṣayaḥ sarve devarṣirnāradastathā|
asito devalo vyāsaḥ svayaṃ caiva bravīṣi me
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: — so all the seers (ṛṣi) call you, and the divine seer Nārada, Asita Devala and Vyāsa; and you yourself tell me so.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'asito devalaḥ' may name one sage (Asita Devala) or two (Asita and Devala). Arjuna grounds his acknowledgement on the testimony of named seers and on Kṛṣṇa's own word.

original.text:
sarvametadṛtaṃ manye yanmāṃ vadasi keśava|
na hi te bhagavan vyakitaṃ vidurdevā na dānavāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: I hold all this true that you tell me, Keśava; for neither the gods nor the Dānavas know your manifestation (vyakti), Blessed One.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The transliteration 'vyakitaṃ' in the segment stands for vyaktim. vyakti: 'manifestation, appearance' — i.e. neither gods nor Dānavas know how/as what the Lord manifests; cf. 10.2.

original.text:
svayamevātmanā'tmānaṃ vettha tvaṃ puruṣottama|
bhūtabhāvana bhūteśa devadeva jagatpate
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: You yourself know yourself by yourself (svayam evātmanātmānaṃ vettha), Supreme Person (puruṣottama), source of beings (bhūtabhāvana), lord of beings, god of gods, lord of the world.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātmanā ātmānam is reflexive here: 'by yourself, yourself'. The point follows from 10.2 and 10.14: none but the Lord knows him.

original.text:
vaktumarhasyaśeṣeṇa divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ|
yābhirvibhūtibhirlokānimāṃstvaṃ vyāpya tiṣṭhasi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: You should tell without remainder your own divine manifestations (ātmavibhūti), the manifestations by which you stand pervading these worlds.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ātma- in ātmavibhūtayaḥ is reflexive: 'your own manifestations'.

original.text:
kathaṃ vidyāmahaṃ yogiṃstvāṃ sadā paricintayan|
keṣu keṣu ca bhāveṣu cintyo'si bhagavanmayā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: How may I know you, yogin, while ever thinking of you (paricintayan)? In which various things/states (bhāva) are you to be thought of by me, Blessed One?
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: This question frames the list of 10.19–41 as supports for continual contemplation (cintya) of the Lord. Arjuna addresses Kṛṣṇa as 'yogin'.

original.text:
vistareṇātmano yogaṃ vibhūtiṃ ca janārdana|
bhūyaḥ kathaya tṛptirhi śrṛṇvato nāsti me'mṛtam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Tell again in detail your own yoga and manifestation (vibhūti), Janārdana; for I am not sated hearing [your] nectar-like [words] (amṛta).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'ātmano yogam' is reflexive ('your own yoga'); 'bhūyaḥ' = again, since 7.8–12 and 9.16–19 already gave such lists. amṛta is the speech that is heard, likened to nectar.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
hanta te kathayiṣyāmi divyā hyātmavibhūtayaḥ|
prādhānyataḥ kuruśreṣṭha nāstyanto vistarasya me
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: Very well, I will tell you my own divine manifestations — by the chief ones (prādhānyataḥ), best of the Kurus; for there is no end to my extent (vistara).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The list will be selective ('by the principal ones'), not exhaustive — restated in 10.40.

original.text:
ahamātmā guḍākeśa sarvabhūtāśayasthitaḥ|
ahamādiśca madhyaṃ ca bhūtānāmanta eva ca
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: I am the self (ātman), Guḍākeśa, abiding in the resting-place (āśaya) of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle and the very end of beings.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: āśaya: 'resting-place, abode', commonly understood as the heart (cf. 18.61 hṛddeśe). ātman here is a noun ('the self'), not reflexive. The commentators divide on the relation stated (identity of the self in all, or the Lord as indwelling self of beings); the verse says only 'I am the self abiding in all beings'.

original.text:
ādityānāmahaṃ viṣṇurjyotiṣāṃ raviraṃśumān|
marīcirmarutāmasmi nakṣatrāṇāmahaṃ śaśī
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of the Ādityas I am Viṣṇu; of lights, the radiant sun; of the Maruts I am Marīci; of the lunar mansions (nakṣatra) I am the moon.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Marīci here is named as one of the Maruts, not the seer Marīci. The list (10.21–38) follows the formula 'of X I am the chief/best one', answering 10.17.

original.text:
vedānāṃ sāmavedo'smi devānāmasmi vāsavaḥ|
indriyāṇāṃ manaścāsmi bhūtānāmasmi cetanā
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of the Vedas I am the Sāmaveda; of the gods I am Vāsava (Indra); of the senses (indriya) I am the mind (manas); in beings I am awareness (cetanā).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: manas is here counted among the senses (indriya) as their chief. cetanā: the sentience/awareness of living beings; kept distinct from citta, cetas, manas and buddhi. bhūtānām may be read 'among beings' or 'of beings'.

original.text:
rudrāṇāṃ śaṅkaraścāsmi vitteśo yakṣarakṣasām|
vasūnāṃ pāvakaścāsmi meruḥ śikhariṇāmaham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of the Rudras I am Śaṅkara; of the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, the lord of wealth (vitteśa, Kubera); of the Vasus I am Pāvaka (fire); of peaked mountains I am Meru.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Śaṅkara here is the name of the chief Rudra (Śiva), not the later teacher.

original.text:
purodhasāṃ ca mukhyaṃ māṃ viddhi pārtha bṛhaspatim|
senānīnāmahaṃ skandaḥ sarasāmasmi sāgaraḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Know me, Pārtha, as the chief of household priests (purodhas), Bṛhaspati; of commanders I am Skanda; of bodies of water I am the ocean.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
maharṣīṇāṃ bhṛgurahaṃ girāmasmyekamakṣaram|
yajñānāṃ japayajño'smi sthāvarāṇāṃ himālayaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of the great seers I am Bhṛgu; of utterances (gir) I am the single syllable (ekam akṣaram); of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of recitation (japa-yajña); of immovable things, the Himālaya.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The verse says only 'the one syllable'; the identification with Oṃ rests on 8.13 ('om ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma') and is the commentators' unanimous reading. Among sacrifices the Lord is japa, the sacrifice of recitation.

original.text:
aśvatthaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ devarṣīṇāṃ ca nāradaḥ|
gandharvāṇāṃ citrarathaḥ siddhānāṃ kapilo muniḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of all trees the aśvattha; of the divine seers (devarṣi), Nārada; of the Gandharvas, Citraratha; of the perfected ones (siddha), the sage (muni) Kapila.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Kapila is named only as 'the muni among the siddhas'; the commentators take him as the Kapila of the Sāṃkhya tradition, which the verse does not state.

original.text:
uccaiḥśravasamaśvānāṃ viddhi māmamṛtodbhavam|
airāvataṃ gajendrāṇāṃ narāṇāṃ ca narādhipam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of horses know me as Uccaiḥśravas, born of the nectar (amṛtodbhava); of lordly elephants, Airāvata; of men, the ruler of men (narādhipa).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: amṛtodbhava: 'arisen with/from the nectar' — the commentators refer it to the churning of the ocean, which the verse does not narrate.

original.text:
āyudhānāmahaṃ vajraṃ dhenūnāmasmi kāmadhuk|
prajanaścāsmi kandarpaḥ sarpāṇāmasmi vāsukiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Of weapons I am the thunderbolt (vajra); of cows, the wish-yielding one (kāmadhuk); I am Kandarpa, the begetter (prajana); of serpents (sarpa) I am Vāsuki.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'prajanaś cāsmi kandarpaḥ': Kandarpa (Kāma) as the cause of begetting — construed by commentators as desire in so far as it produces offspring. sarpa (here) and nāga (10.29) are distinguished by the text; the commentators explain the difference variously.

original.text:
anantaścāsmi nāgānāṃ varuṇo yādasāmaham|
pitṛ़ṇāmaryamā cāsmi yamaḥ saṃyamatāmaham

paraphrase: Chapter 10 (vibhūti). Movements: (1) 10.1–11 — the Lord resumes his supreme word for Arjuna's good: neither gods nor seers know his origin, since he is their origin (10.2); knowing him as unborn and beginningless frees from sin (10.3); the states of beings arise from him alone (10.4–5); the seers and Manus born of mind share his being (10.6); knowing his vibhūti and yoga in truth joins one to unwavering yoga (10.7); the wise worship him as the source of all, with citta and prāṇa given to him, speaking of him to one another (10.8–9); to them he gives buddhiyoga and, out of compassion, destroys the darkness of ignorance with the lamp of knowledge (10.10–11). (2) 10.12–18 — Arjuna acknowledges him as the supreme brahman, supreme abode and first god, as the seers Nārada, Asita Devala and Vyāsa declared, and asks to hear his self-manifestations in full, so as to know in which things he is to be contemplated (10.17). (3) 10.19–39 — the list of manifestations 'by the chief ones': the self in all beings and their beginning, middle and end (10.20), then the pre-eminent member of class after class — gods, seers, Vedas, the mind among the senses, awareness in beings, the single syllable, japa, time, death, the letter A, silence, knowledge — ending with the Lord as the seed of all beings (10.39). (4) 10.40–42 — there is no end to them; whatever is glorious springs from a portion of his splendour; he stands supporting the whole world with a single portion. Purpose as the chapter states it: that Arjuna, who delights in hearing, may know the Lord's vibhūti and yoga in truth (10.1, 10.7) and have supports for contemplating him (10.17).
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The chapter has no colophon in this edition's segments. The list verses (10.21–38) each record several manifestations; each is its own entry.

original.text:
tvamakṣaraṃ paramaṃ veditavyaṃ
tvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam|
tvamavyayaḥ śāśvatadharmagoptā
sanātanastvaṃ puruṣo mato me

paraphrase: You are the imperishable (akṣara), the highest, that which is to be known; you are the supreme resting-place (nidhāna) of this universe; you are the undecaying (avyaya) guardian of the eternal dharma; you are, I hold, the ancient person (sanātana puruṣa).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Here akṣara is an epithet of the Lord seen in the form (cf. 8.3 'akṣaraṃ brahma paramam'); contrast 12.1–3, where the akṣara is named as a distinct object of worship. 'śāśvatadharmagoptā': guardian of the eternal dharma.

original.text:
anādimadhyāntamanantavīrya
manantabāhuṃ śaśisūryanetram|
paśyāmi tvāṃ dīptahutāśavaktram
svatejasā viśvamidaṃ tapantam

paraphrase: I see you without beginning, middle or end, of endless might, of endless arms, the moon and sun your eyes, your mouth a blazing sacrificial fire (hutāśa), heating this universe with your own splendour.
speaker: Arjuna

original.text:
dyāvāpṛthivyoridamantaraṃ hi
vyāptaṃ tvayaikena diśaśca sarvāḥ|
dṛṣṭvā'dbhutaṃ rūpamugraṃ tavedaṃ
lokatrayaṃ pravyathitaṃ mahātman

paraphrase: For this space between heaven and earth, and all the directions, are pervaded by you alone; seeing this wondrous, terrible (ugra) form of yours, great one (mahātman), the three worlds tremble.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
amī hi tvāṃ surasaṅghāḥ viśanti
kecidbhītāḥ prāñjalayo gṛṇanti|
svastītyuktvā maharṣisiddhasaṅghāḥ
stuvanti tvāṃ stutibhiḥ puṣkalābhiḥ

paraphrase: For these hosts of gods enter into you; some, afraid, praise you with joined palms; saying 'svasti' ('may it be well'), the hosts of great seers and perfected ones (siddha) praise you with abundant hymns.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
rudrādityā vasavo ye ca sādhyā
viśve'śivanau marutaścoṣmapāśca|
gandharvayakṣāsurasiddhasaṅghā
vīkṣante tvāṃ vismitāścaiva sarve

paraphrase: The Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus and Sādhyas, the Viśve[devas], the two Aśvins, the Maruts and the steam-drinkers (ūṣmapa), and the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Asuras and perfected ones (siddha) — all gaze at you in amazement.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ūṣmapāḥ, 'steam/heat-drinkers', are taken by the commentators as the ancestors (pitṛ). The segment's 'aśivanau' stands for aśvinau.

original.text:
rūpaṃ mahatte bahuvaktranetraṃ
mahābāho bahubāhūrupādam|
bahūdaraṃ bahudaṃṣṭrākarālaṃ
dṛṣṭvā lokāḥ pravyathitāstathā'ham
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Seeing your great form, mighty-armed one, with many mouths and eyes, many arms, thighs and feet, many bellies, terrible with many tusks, the worlds tremble, and so do I.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
nabhaḥspṛśaṃ dīptamanekavarṇaṃ
vyāttānanaṃ dīptaviśālanetram|
dṛṣṭvā hi tvāṃ pravyathitāntarātmā
dhṛtiṃ na vindāmi śamaṃ ca viṣṇo
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Seeing you touching the sky, blazing, many-coloured, with gaping mouths and huge blazing eyes, I — shaken in my inmost being (pravyathita-antarātman) — find neither steadiness (dhṛti) nor calm (śama), Viṣṇu.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: antarātman here is 'inner being' (Arjuna's own), used of his shaken state; no doctrine of the self is being stated. Arjuna addresses Kṛṣṇa as Viṣṇu.

original.text:
daṃṣṭrākarālāni ca te mukhāni
dṛṣṭvaiva kālānalasannibhāni|
diśo na jāne na labhe ca śarma
prasīda deveśa jagannivāsa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Having seen your mouths, terrible with tusks, like the fire of time (kālānala), I do not know the directions and I find no shelter (śarman). Be gracious (prasīda), lord of gods, abode of the world.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: kālānala: the fire of (the end of) time — commentators: the fire that consumes the worlds at their dissolution.

original.text:
amī ca tvāṃ dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāḥ
sarve sahaivāvanipālasaṅghaiḥ|
bhīṣmo droṇaḥ sūtaputrastathā'sau
sahāsmadīyairapi yodhamukhyaiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: And all these sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with hosts of kings, Bhīṣma, Droṇa and that son of the charioteer (sūtaputra), together with our own chief warriors too —
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Sentence continues in 11.27. sūtaputra, 'son of the charioteer', is Karṇa (named in 11.34). 'asmadīyaiḥ' — warriors of Arjuna's own side are also seen entering.

original.text:
vaktrāṇi te tvaramāṇā viśanti
daṃṣṭrākarālāni bhayānakāni|
kecidvilagnā daśanāntareṣu
saṃdṛśyante cūrṇitairuttamāṅgaiḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: — rush hurrying into your mouths, terrible with tusks and fearful; some are seen stuck between the teeth, their heads crushed to powder.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yathā nadīnāṃ bahavo'mbuvegāḥ
samudramevābhimukhāḥ dravanti|
tathā tavāmī naralokavīrā
viśanti vaktrāṇyabhivijvalanti
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: As the many torrents of rivers run toward the ocean alone, so these heroes of the world of men enter your blazing mouths.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
yathā pradīptaṃ jvalanaṃ pataṅgā
viśanti nāśāya samṛddhavegāḥ|
tathaiva nāśāya viśanti lokā
stavāpi vaktrāṇi samṛddhavegāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: As moths rush with swelling speed into a blazing fire to perish, so too the worlds (lokāḥ) rush with swelling speed into your mouths to perish.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: The two similes (rivers to the sea, 11.28; moths to the flame, 11.29) are read by some commentators as contrasting unwitting and willing entry into destruction; the verses themselves only juxtapose them. lokāḥ here = peoples/worlds.

original.text:
lelihyase grasamānaḥ samantā
llokānsamagrānvadanairjvaladbhiḥ|
tejobhirāpūrya jagatsamagraṃ
bhāsastavogrāḥ pratapanti viṣṇo

original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Devouring all the worlds on every side with flaming mouths, you lick [your lips]; filling the whole world with splendour, your fierce rays burn, Viṣṇu.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
ākhyāhi me ko bhavānugrarūpo
namo'stu te devavara prasīda|
vijñātumicchāmi bhavantamādyaṃ
na hi prajānāmi tava pravṛttim
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Tell me who you are, of fierce form. Homage to you, best of gods; be gracious. I wish to know you, the primal one (ādya), for I do not understand what you are doing (pravṛtti).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: pravṛtti: 'activity, undertaking, purpose' — Arjuna does not understand what the form is engaged in; answered in 11.32.

original.text:
śrī bhagavānuvāca
kālo'smi lokakṣayakṛtpravṛddho
lokānsamāhartumiha pravṛttaḥ|
ṛte'pi tvāṃ na bhaviṣyanti sarve
ye'vasthitāḥ pratyanīkeṣu yodhāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: The Blessed Lord said: I am Time (kāla), grown mighty (pravṛddha), the maker of the destruction of worlds, engaged here in drawing in the worlds (lokān samāhartum). Even without you, all these warriors drawn up in the opposing ranks shall cease to be.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: ṛte 'pi tvām: 'even without you' — i.e. even without Arjuna's act. pratyanīkeṣu: 'in the opposing/facing ranks'; commentators differ on whether warriors of both armies are meant. Cf. 10.30, 10.33 (the Lord as time) and 10.34 (as death).

original.text:
tasmāttvamuttiṣṭha yaśo labhasva
jitvā śatrūn bhuṅkṣva rājyaṃ samṛddham|
mayaivaite nihatāḥ pūrvameva
nimittamātraṃ bhava savyasācin
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Therefore stand up and win glory; conquering your enemies, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By me alone they have already been slain; be merely the instrument (nimitta-mātra), left-handed archer (savyasācin).
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: nimitta: 'instrument' or 'occasion, apparent cause'. The injunction ('tasmāt', therefore) is drawn from the fact stated in 11.32: the deaths are already accomplished by the Lord; Arjuna is to act as the instrument. The verse also names worldly results (glory, kingdom).

original.text:
droṇaṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca jayadrathaṃ ca
karṇaṃ tathā'nyānapi yodhavīrān|
mayā hatāṃstvaṃ jahi mā vyathiṣṭhā
yudhyasva jetāsi raṇe sapatnān
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Droṇa and Bhīṣma, Jayadratha and Karṇa, and the other heroic warriors too, already slain by me — do you slay them; do not be distressed (mā vyathiṣṭhāḥ); fight: you will conquer your rivals in battle.
speaker: Kṛṣṇa
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Names four warriors of the opposing side, two of them Arjuna's elders/teachers (Bhīṣma, Droṇa), linking the vision back to Arjuna's refusal in ch. 1–2.

original.text:
etacchrutvā vacanaṃ keśavasya
kṛtāñjalirvepamānaḥ kirīṭī|
namaskṛtvā bhūya evāha kṛṣṇaṃ
sagadgadaṃ bhītabhītaḥ praṇamya
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Sañjaya said: Hearing this word of Keśava, the crowned one (Kirīṭin), with joined palms, trembling, did homage; and bowing low, stammering and in great fear, he spoke again to Kṛṣṇa.
speaker: Sañjaya
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
sthāne hṛṣīkeśa tava prakīrtyā
jagat prahṛṣyatyanurajyate ca|
rakṣāṃsi bhītāni diśo dravanti
sarve namasyanti ca siddhasaṅghāḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)

paraphrase: Arjuna said: Fittingly (sthāne), Hṛṣīkeśa, does the world rejoice and delight in your praise (prakīrti); the Rākṣasas flee in fear in all directions, and all the hosts of the perfected (siddha) bow down.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prakīrtyā: 'by/at your praise (glorification)' or 'in your renown'. The hymn of 11.36–44 begins here.

original.text:
kasmācca te na nameranmahātman
garīyase brahmaṇo'pyādikartre|
ananta deveśa jagannivāsa
tvamakṣaraṃ sadasattatparaṃ yat
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: And why should they not bow to you, great one, who are weightier [than all] and the first maker — even of Brahmā? Endless one, lord of gods, abode of the world, you are the imperishable (akṣara): being and non-being (sad-asat), and that which is beyond.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Two construals are open. (1) brahmaṇaḥ may go with garīyase ('weightier even than Brahmā/brahman') or with ādikartre ('first maker even of Brahmā'). (2) 'tvam akṣaraṃ sad asat tat paraṃ yat' may be read 'you are the imperishable, being and non-being, and what is beyond [them]' or 'you are the imperishable which is beyond being and non-being' (cf. 13.13 in this edition = 13.12 vulgate: 'na sat tan nāsad ucyate'). The paraphrase keeps the minimal shared sense.

original.text:
tvamādidevaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇa
stvamasya viśvasya paraṃ nidhānam|
vettāsi vedyaṃ ca paraṃ ca dhāma
tvayā tataṃ viśvamanantarūpa
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: You are the first god, the ancient person (puruṣa purāṇa); you are the supreme resting-place (nidhāna) of this universe; you are the knower and what is to be known, and the supreme abode (param dhāma); by you this universe is spread out (tata), you of endless form.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
vāyuryamo'gnirvaruṇaḥ śaśāṅkaḥ
prajāpatistvaṃ prapitāmahaśca|
namo namaste'stu sahasrakṛtvaḥ
punaśca bhūyo'pi namo namaste
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: You are Vāyu, Yama, Agni, Varuṇa, the moon (śaśāṅka), Prajāpati and the great-grandsire (prapitāmaha). Homage, homage to you a thousand times, and yet again, once more, homage, homage to you!
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: prapitāmaha: 'great-grandsire' — commentators: the father even of Brahmā the grandsire. The repeated 'namo namaḥ' is an act of homage within the hymn.

original.text:
namaḥ purastādatha pṛṣṭhataste
namo'stu te sarvata eva sarva|
anantavīryāmitavikramastvaṃ
sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato'si sarvaḥ
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Homage to you in front and behind; homage to you on every side, O All (sarva)! Of endless might and immeasurable prowess, you pervade (samāpnoṣi) all; therefore you are all.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'sarvaṃ samāpnoṣi tato 'si sarvaḥ': you are 'all' because you pervade all — a reason is given (tataḥ). The commentators construe the identity differently (the Lord as the self of all, or as named 'all' because he pervades all); the verse gives only the inference.

original.text:
sakheti matvā prasabhaṃ yaduktaṃ
he kṛṣṇa he yādava he sakheti|
ajānatā mahimānaṃ tavedaṃ
mayā pramādātpraṇayena vāpi
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: Whatever I said rashly, thinking [you] a friend — 'O Kṛṣṇa, O Yādava, O friend' — not knowing this greatness of yours, through heedlessness (pramāda) or even through affection (praṇaya) —
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Sentence continues in 11.42 (the request for forgiveness).

original.text:
yaccāvahāsārthamasatkṛto'si
vihāraśayyāsanabhojaneṣu|
eko'thavāpyacyuta tatsamakṣaṃ
tatkṣāmaye tvāmahamaprameyam
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: — and if, for the sake of jest, you were treated without respect while at play, lying down, sitting or eating, alone or in the presence of others, Acyuta — for that I ask forgiveness of you, the immeasurable (aprameya).
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted

original.text:
pitāsi lokasya carācarasya
tvamasya pūjyaśca gururgarīyān|
na tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ kuto'nyo
lokatraye'pyapratimaprabhāva
original.edition: Sanskrit text from github.com/gita/gita data/verse.json (vulgate; 701 entries incl. the extra verse at the start of ch. 13 found in some editions)
original.licence: public domain (Sanskrit root text); source repository under the Unlicense

paraphrase: You are the father of the world, of the moving and the unmoving; you are its object of worship (pūjya) and its weightiest teacher (guru). There is none equal to you — how then any greater? — even in the three worlds, you of incomparable power.
speaker: Arjuna
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: 'gurur garīyān' may be read 'the weightier/greatest guru' or as two predicates ('the guru, the weightier one').

original.text:
tasmātpraṇamya praṇidhāya kāyaṃ
prasādaye tvāmahamīśamīḍyam|

paraphrase: Chapter 11 (the vision of the universal form). Movements: (1) 11.1–4 — Arjuna says his delusion is gone through the teaching and asks, if possible, to see the Lord's sovereign form. (2) 11.5–8 — the Lord bids him behold his countless forms and the whole world standing as one in his body, and gives him a divine eye, since it cannot be seen with ordinary sight. (3) 11.9–14 — Sañjaya tells Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the form shown: many mouths and eyes, divine ornaments and weapons, a radiance like a thousand suns, the world standing as one in the god's body; Arjuna, amazed and with hair on end, bows. (4) 11.15–31 — Arjuna's account of what he sees: the gods and beings within the form; a form without beginning, middle or end; the imperishable, the resting-place of the universe (11.18); the worlds trembling; the warriors of both sides rushing into its mouths like rivers to the sea and moths to the flame; he asks who this fierce one is. (5) 11.32–34 — the Lord answers that he is Time, destroyer of worlds; the warriors are already slain by him; Arjuna is to be merely the instrument and fight. (6) 11.35–46 — trembling, Arjuna praises him (11.36–40), asks forgiveness for past familiarity (11.41–44), and, thrilled and afraid, asks to see the former four-armed form. (7) 11.47–51 — the Lord says the form was shown by his grace and his own yoga and is not attainable by Vedas, sacrifice, study, gifts, rites or austerity; he bids Arjuna not fear, resumes his gentle form, and Arjuna regains composure. (8) 11.52–55 — the form is rare even for gods; by undivided devotion alone can he be known, seen in truth and entered; the one who does his work, holds him highest, is devoted, unattached and without enmity comes to him. Purpose as the chapter presents it: to grant the sight Arjuna asked for (11.3–4), to reveal the Lord as Time directing the battle (11.32–34), and to state the means by which he is seen and reached (11.54–55).
translation_basis: own paraphrase made directly from the Sanskrit text; no published translation consulted
notes: Speaker changes: Arjuna 11.1–4, the Lord 11.5–8, Sañjaya 11.9–14, Arjuna 11.15–31, the Lord 11.32–34, Sañjaya 11.35, Arjuna 11.36–46, the Lord 11.47–49, Sañjaya 11.50, Arjuna 11.51, the Lord 11.52–55.

paraphrase: For knowledge (jñāna) is better than practice (abhyāsa); meditation (dhyāna) is superior to knowledge; relinquishment of the fruit of actions (karmaphalatyāga) [is superior] to meditation; from relinquishment (tyāga), peace (śānti) follows immediately.

The verse itself gives the ground: peace follows relinquishment immediately.

paraphrase: But those who, with faith (śraddhā), holding me as the highest (matparama), attend to (paryupāsate) this nectar of dharma (dharmyāmṛta) as it has been declared — those devotees are exceedingly dear to me.

notes: Closes the chapter: those who follow with faith 'this' (the qualities just described, or the whole teaching of the chapter) are 'exceedingly dear' (atīva priyāḥ) — a step beyond the refrain 'dear' of 12.14–19. dharmyāmṛtam: 'the nectar consisting in dharma' or 'the dharma that leads to immortality'.

paraphrase: Chapter 12 (devotion). Movements: (1) 12.1 — Arjuna asks which are the better knowers of yoga: the devotees ever joined who worship Kṛṣṇa as just described (11.55), or those who worship the imperishable unmanifest. (2) 12.2–5 — the Lord's answer: those who fix their manas on him and worship him with supreme faith are held the most joined; those who worship the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging — with senses restrained, even-minded and delighting in the welfare of all beings, also reach him; but the hardship is greater for them, since the unmanifest goal is reached with pain by the embodied. (3) 12.6–7 — those who renounce all actions in him and meditate on him with undivided yoga he lifts before long from the ocean of death and saṃsāra. (4) 12.8–12 — a conditional sequence: fix manas and buddhi on him; if unable, seek him by the yoga of practice; if unable, be intent on work for him; if unable, relinquish the fruit of all actions; followed by the ranking of knowledge over practice, meditation over knowledge, relinquishment over meditation, and peace immediately from relinquishment. (5) 12.13–19 — the marks of the devotee dear to the Lord: without hatred, friendly and compassionate, without 'mine' and 'I', even in pleasure and pain, content, restrained, neither troubling nor troubled by the world, free of elation, impatience, fear and agitation, without expectation, the same to friend and foe, in honour and dishonour, praise and blame, silent, homeless, steady, full of devotion — each group closing with 'he is dear to me'. (6) 12.20 — those who with faith follow this nectar of dharma, holding him highest, are exceedingly dear. Purpose as the chapter presents it: to answer which worshippers are the best knowers of yoga (12.1–2) and to lay out graded means and the marks of the devotee (12.8–20).
